IAMA high school and college drop out. AMA.
Why did you go to college if you dropped out of high school?

Same reason everyone else does I think. You're expected to, and you think it'll get you a better job. So I got my GED and went. Don't get me wrong, a degree will get your foot in the door for better jobs, but it takes more than that. Connections and luck are just as important.

I agree, I also dropped out of college. It just seemed odd to me that you would drop out of high school and be like "now that I quit high school, i think ill try this other more difficult school and it should be better there" I am just interested in what thought process you had before making the decision to go back to college after leaving highschool. Were there circumstances that arose you to be forced to peruse a GED as opposed to a high school degree? Or did you make the conscious decision to leave high school to get your GED with the purpose of going to college?

Edit: where to were

I wasn't forced out of high school per se, but there were guys sexually harassing me. I really couldn't stand it. I think now that I should have transferred instead of completely dropping out, but I knew I couldn't stay there.

That sucks (the harassment part). We don't all make optimal decisions, even as adults. I'm not in any way saying you will be unsuccessful because of the path you chose. I was simply curious to your process. Good luck in your future and i wish you good fortune.

To be fair, there is a difference between high school and college. I hated high school - repetitive, disruptive, and controlled. I took college classes my sophomore/junior year of high school and it was enlightening. Not that everything annoying about high school was fixed in college, but the level of annoyance was manageable.

Personally, I am of the opinion that the difference is that 1) you can pick up and leave in college and 2) people tend not to value anything that they aren't paying for.
What's your advice for other high-school dropouts, as in should they at least attempt furthering their education, etc.?

Get a GED. First thing after you drop out, get your GED. A lot of temp agencies in my area will turn you away without at least a GED. It just makes life easier.

If you are really interested in a subject and have the time and money, maybe try your hand at a community college.

Otherwise I would really recommend getting certified in a trade like welding or electrical work if you've got the skill and the will.

Definitely try and build a good resume though. Put some experience on your resume, even if it's irrelevant to where you want to go.
What college accepted a high school drop out?
As long as the scores on the placement exam meet the minimum criteria for the schools gen ed curriculum, they'll take you. Unless the school has a stick up its ass, like the Ivy schools, to name 5.

I went to a community college at first. I was there for a year before I thought I could do better. I had a fair GPA, about 3.5. I applied at a university and was admitted. It just cost way too much, so I decided to leave to focus on making money. Never went back.
Are you happy with your decision to drop out?

Not really. It really fucked me over in the long run. I could have been well on my way to a doctorate in psychology at this point. But to be honest I am glad I didn't go through with psychology. I'm not as interested in it as I was while I was there.

I still live with my parents. I work part time in a store and do computer work for people on the side. I pay a few bills, pat for my own phone, but on only my income I'd only be able to afford a shitty apartment.
Computer work is a good way to make some money, everybody has at least one computer at home. Keep it up!

In high school I was being sexually harassed by other guys. They were grabbing my ass. I couldn't take it so I dropped out

In college I left to focus on making money. Never went back.
you seem young enough to 'put your life on hold' for a couple years, why not go back and finish college?

A lot of the classes I took were needed for most degrees, but some were specific for a psychology degree. They could be applied as a social science I think. Anyway, I have. Only instead of finishing my degree I was thinking about getting a 2 year degree in networking or IT.
What are the biggest pros and cons about having dropped out?

Well the biggest pro would be being able to get your GED before your friends and high school class graduate. I remember the GED test was really easy. Of course this was a few years ago so things mat have changed. I remember hearing that last year in my state the test was made tougher.

Of course there are downsides. First is that some people think of you differently when they find out that you dropped out or have a GED. They think you're stupid.

That can even apply to employers too. I've only let it slip in a couple interviews, but they respond the same. A sort of disappointed "oh" and then some variation of "we'll let you know if we need you"

Hello. I'm someone who doesn't believe that college is worth the money these days when vocations pay as well as school teacher jobs. I do plan on finishing high school, but not going to college. Any tips you could give to someone who is taking my path? I know it's not the same you took but I figure you have some knowledge.

Be proactive about your future. At the very least start learning the basics of the skill(s) you want to work with. Maybe consider shadowing someone in the profession you want to get into, making friends in the industry at the same time. Connections are just as important for most jobs that do not require a degree as they are for ones that do.

Right now, get my CompTIA A+ certification to bolster my resume. I'm trying to get a job in the IT field, and the ones that don't require a degree require a cert.
